items.title: Section: Doing Evil Without Delighting in It, and Delighting in Evil Without Doing It

items.zh: 復有四種補特伽羅。或有行惡而非樂惡，或有樂惡而非行惡，或有行惡亦復樂惡，或非行惡亦非樂惡。若信諸惡能感當來非愛果報，由失念故、或放逸故、近惡友故、造作惡行，是名行惡而非樂惡。若先世來串習惡故，喜樂諸惡，惡欲所牽，彼由親近善丈夫故、聞正法故、如理作意為依止故，見諸惡行能感當來非愛果報，自勉自勵遠離諸惡，是名樂惡而非行惡。若性樂惡而不遠離，是名行惡亦復樂惡。若有為性不樂諸惡，亦能遠離，名非行惡亦非樂惡。此中行惡亦樂惡者，是名下士；若有行惡而非樂惡，或有樂惡而非行惡，是名中士；若非行惡亦非樂惡，是名上士。
items.en: There are also four kinds of person. Some do evil yet do not delight in it; some delight in evil yet do not do it; some both do evil and delight in it; and some neither do evil nor delight in it. If one believes evils bring about undesirable future results, yet through lost mindfulness, heedlessness, or nearness to bad friends, commits evil conduct, this is called doing evil without delighting in it. If, habituated to evil since past lives, one delights in evils, drawn by evil desire, yet, through nearness to a good person, hearing correct teaching, and relying on correct attention, sees that evil conduct brings undesirable future results, and exerts effort to distance oneself from evil, this is called delighting in evil without doing it. If one is by nature inclined to evil and does not distance from it, this is called both doing evil and delighting in it. If one is by nature not inclined to evil and is able to distance from it, this is called neither doing evil nor delighting in it. Among these, one who both does evil and delights in it is called a lower person; one who does evil without delighting in it, or delights in evil without doing it, is called a middling person; and one who neither does evil nor delights in it is called a superior person.

items.title: Section: What a Person Values Most, and a King's Three Kinds of Completeness

items.zh: 復有三士。一、重受欲，二、重事務，三、重正法。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又有三種補特伽羅。一、以非事為自事，二、以自事為自事，三、以他事為自事。若行惡行以自存活，名以非事為自事；若怖惡行，修行善行，名以自事為自事；若諸菩薩，名以他事為自事。等。初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。又諸國王有三圓滿，謂果報圓滿、士用圓滿、功德圓滿。若諸國王生富貴家，長壽少病，有大宗葉，成就俱生聰利之慧，是王名為果報圓滿。若諸國王善權方便所攝持故，恒常成就圓滿英勇，是王名為士用圓滿。若諸國王任持正法，名為法王；安住正法，名為大王。與內宮王子、群臣、英傑、豪貴、國人，共修惠施、樹福、受齋、堅持禁戒，是王名為功德圓滿。
items.en: There are also three kinds of person: valuing desire, valuing enterprise, and valuing the true Dharma. The first is a lower person, the second a middling person, the third a superior person. There are also three kinds of person: treating improper deeds as one's affair, treating one's own affair as one's affair, and treating another's affair as one's affair. Sustaining oneself through evil conduct is treating improper deeds as one's affair. Fearing evil conduct and cultivating wholesome conduct is treating one's own affair as one's affair. A bodhisattva treating another's affair as one's own affair. The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. Kings also have three kinds of completeness: completeness of ripened result, completeness of capability, and completeness of virtue. A king born into wealth and nobility, long-lived and rarely ill, of an accomplished lineage, possessing innate wisdom, has completeness of ripened result. A king who, through skilful means, constantly accomplishes full heroism, has completeness of capability. A king who sustains the true Dharma, called a dharma-king, or abides in it, called a great king, and together with the royal household, ministers, the eminent, the noble, and the people, practices giving, cultivates merit, observes fasting days, and firmly keeps the precepts, has completeness of virtue.

items.title: Section: Three Fruits for Three Kinds of King, and Three Kinds of Minister

items.zh: 果報圓滿者，受用先世淨業果報。士用圓滿者，受用現法可愛之果。功德圓滿者，亦於當來受用圓滿淨業果報。若有國王，三種圓滿皆不具足，名為下士；若有果報圓滿，或士用圓滿，或俱圓滿，名為中士；若三圓滿無不具足，名為上士。復有三臣。一、有忠信，無伎能、智慧；二、有忠信、伎能，無智慧；三、具忠信、伎能、智慧。
items.en: Completeness of ripened result is enjoying the fruit of pure karma cultivated in a past life. Completeness of capability is enjoying the beloved fruit of this present life. Completeness of virtue is likewise enjoying, in the future, the complete fruit of pure karma. A king lacking all three completenesses is a lower person; one with ripened result, or capability, or both, is a middling person; one lacking none of the three completenesses is a superior person. There are also three kinds of minister. First, one loyal and trustworthy, but without skill or wisdom. Second, one loyal, trustworthy, and skilled, but without wisdom. Third, one possessing loyalty, skill, and wisdom together.

items.title: Section: Four Kinds of Speech, Sharp and Sweet

items.zh: 初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。若不忠信，無有伎能，亦無智慧，當知此臣下中之下。又有四語。一、非愛似愛，二、愛似非愛，三、非愛似非愛，四、愛似愛。諸有語言辭句善順，然非所宜，是名初語。或有語言辭句勃逆，然是所宜，是第二語。或有語言辭句勃逆，亦非所宜，是第三語。或有語言辭句善順，亦是所宜，是第四語。若有宣說非愛似非愛、非愛似愛語者，是下士；若有宣說愛似非愛語者，是中士；若有宣說愛似愛語者，是上士。
items.en: The first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior. One lacking loyalty, skill, and wisdom alike is lower than the lowest. There are also four kinds of speech: unloving-seeming-loving, loving-seeming-unloving, unloving-seeming-unloving, and loving-seeming-loving. Speech whose words are smooth and pleasing, yet not truly helpful, is the first. Speech whose words are harsh, yet truly helpful, is the second. Speech whose words are harsh and also unhelpful is the third. Speech whose words are smooth and also truly helpful is the fourth. One who speaks the unloving-seeming-unloving or unloving-seeming-loving kind is a lower person; one who speaks the loving-seeming-unloving kind is a middling person; one who speaks the loving-seeming-loving kind is a superior person.

items.title: Section: Three Ways of Enjoying Wealth and Desire

items.zh: 復有三種受諸欲者。或有受欲，非法孟浪積集財寶，不能安樂正養己身及與妻子，廣說乃至不於沙門、婆羅門所修殖福田。或有受欲，法或非法、孟浪或非積集財寶，能以安樂正養己身、妻子、眷屬及知友等，不於沙門、婆羅門所修殖福田。或有受欲，一向以法及不孟浪積集財寶，能以安樂正養己身，廣說乃至能於沙門、婆羅門所修殖福田。此三種中，初名下士，次名中士，後名上士。
items.en: There are also three kinds of persons who enjoy desire. One gathers wealth unlawfully and recklessly, unable to properly support themselves and their spouse, let alone give to renunciants and brahmins as a field of merit. One gathers wealth by lawful or unlawful, reckless or careful means, able to support themselves, their spouse, their family, and their friends, yet gives nothing to renunciants and brahmins. One gathers wealth exclusively by lawful and careful means, able to properly support themselves, and also gives to renunciants and brahmins. Of these three, the first is a lower person, the second middling, the third superior.

blocks.text: A run of short sūtras on three grades of people: lower, middling, and superior.
Master Cháng Bǎi: though much evil was done in past lives, after hearing the true teaching one knows evil brings undesirable results, and does not delight in it.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the third person especially values practice and study of the Dharma. Some make evil their business; the bodhisattva takes others' pains and joys as their own. A king who sustains the true Dharma is a "dharma king"; one who merely abides in it, a "great king".
Happy in the past life, this life, and the next. Master Cháng Bǎi: a minister lacking loyalty, talent, and wisdom is the lowest.
Master Cháng Bǎi: some speech has a good motive but a manner hard to take: the treatise ranks this "middling". Honeyed words over a bad heart are unloving speech that only seems loving.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the best person gathers wealth lawfully and carefully, cares for family and friends, and also gives to ascetics and brahmins.
"Unloving, though it seems loving." Flattery is listed as a fault of speech, not a kindness.

quiz.q: Why does one who delights in evil not do it, and which person is this?
options: one merely lacks the chance while still wanting to, and so is a lower person
fear of the law; a superior person
despite past habit, through the true teaching and right reflection one restrains oneself; a middling person
seeds are severed; a superior person
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: though much evil was done in past lives, after hearing the true teaching and relying on right reflection, one knows evil brings undesirable results and urges oneself not to do it. The treatise ranks this person as middling.

quiz.q: How do valuing desire, enterprise, and the true Dharma map onto the three persons?
options: desire is lower, enterprise is middling, and the true Dharma is superior
enterprise is lower and desire middling, the busy having less wisdom than the pleasure-seeking
all three are middling
the Dharma is lower, there being no fruit yet
quiz.why: The order is explicit in the treatise. Master Cháng Bǎi on the third: this person especially values practice, enjoys studying the Dharma, and gives weight to the path and to training the mind. Enterprise ranks above desire.

quiz.q: 以非事為自事 is rendered "treating what is not one's affair as one's affair." Why might it blur with the third person?
options: 非事 is evil that should not be done, yet the English sounds like minding others' business
no blurring: 非事 means others' affairs, the two differing only in motive, as the lecture says
"affair" should be "romance"
"one's" should be deleted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one who lives by killing, stealing, and the like makes evil one's business; the bodhisattva takes others' affairs, pains, and joys as one's own. The English label for the first could be misread as meddling, close to the third.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish sustaining from abiding in the true Dharma?
options: sustaining is one's own practice and abiding is teaching others, so the sustainer is the great king
there is no difference
sustaining is precepts, abiding is meditation
sustaining also means keeping the Dharma going beyond abiding, and abiding means settling the mind in it
quiz.why: The treatise names the sustainer a dharma-king and the one abiding a great king. Master Cháng Bǎi: sustaining goes beyond abiding, keeping the true Dharma going, while abiding is settling the mind in it. Option B reverses the two titles.

quiz.q: In which time does each of a king's three completenesses enjoy its fruit?
options: all three enjoy fruit in the next life, since a king's deeds ripen only then
all three from past lives
ripened result enjoys past pure karma, capability this life's fruit, and virtue the fruit of pure karma in the future
ripened result now, capability from the past
quiz.why: Past, present, and future line up with the three. Master Cháng Bǎi: happy in the previous life, in this life, and surely in the next, because pure karma is cultivated before and now. He explains the present fruit through diligent rule.

quiz.q: What is a king's completeness of capability, in Master Cháng Bǎi's words?
options: good past karma makes him rich and long-lived with no effort, the reward of his birth
he keeps precepts with the people
he has a great lineage
he is diligent in government in this life, not heedless, clear in rewards and penalties, and gains the beloved fruit now
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: it means the king is diligent in government, not heedless, and clear in rewards and penalties, so he gains beloved results now; his function as king is developed to the full. Option B is ripened result, C is virtue.

quiz.q: By what standard are the three ministers, and the one "lower than the lowest," judged?
options: by rank in court
by the size of the salary
by loyalty, skill, and wisdom: loyalty alone is lower, with skill middling, all three superior, and none at all lowest
by family background
quiz.why: The three grades are cumulative, always starting with loyalty. Master Cháng Bǎi: one lacking all three, unreliable and without talent or wisdom, not knowing good and evil karma, is lower still within the lowest. Rank and pay play no part.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain speech that loves yet seems unloving, and which person is this?
options: the motive is bad but the words sweet, a skilled speaker; a superior person
the motive is good, while the manner is hard to bear; a middling person
both are good; superior
both are bad; lower
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the motive is good, but the manner of expression is hard to take. The treatise ranks this speaker as middling. Honeyed words over a bad heart are unloving-seeming-loving, which he calls a lower person's speech.

quiz.q: Among the four speeches, which is smooth in words yet not truly helpful?
options: loving-seeming-unloving, being pleasant though unsuited to the moment
unloving-seeming-unloving
loving-seeming-loving
unloving-seeming-loving
quiz.why: The first of the four is unloving-seeming-loving. Master Cháng Bǎi: one merely follows the other's wishes; the content is not loving, though on the surface it sounds so. It is thus ranked with a lower person's speech.

quiz.q: §28 has "unloving-seeming-unloving" in the list but "unloving-unhelpful" in the ranking. What is the problem?
options: none: the Chinese itself varies between the two, as the lecture points out
one term gets two renderings, and manner of speech is mixed up with helpfulness
it should be "loving-helpful"
"kind" should be deleted
quiz.why: The Chinese uses the same term both times, so the English should as well. Master Cháng Bǎi: at heart one does not care for the other, and the words also make one uncomfortable. "Unhelpful" answers 所宜, a different layer from 似.

quiz.q: The third enjoyer is rendered "able to properly support themselves, and also gives ..." What problem does the omission cause?
options: none: this person supports only themselves and gives, leaving out family, as the lecture says
婆羅門 is lost
財寶 is lost
廣說乃至 covers family and friends, so without it the person seems to support only themselves
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this person gathers wealth lawfully and carefully and also gives to ascetics and brahmins. The Chinese 廣說乃至 abbreviates the earlier list of spouse, children, family, and friends, which the English simply deletes.

quiz.q: How does the second enjoyer of desire differ from the third?
options: the second cannot feed the household, spending everything on sacrifices, and is thus middling
the second is a monk
the third gathers no wealth
the second gathers lawfully or not and gives no merit-gift; the third is wholly lawful and gives to ascetics
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the second gathers wealth by lawful or unlawful, reckless or careful means, and cares well for household and friends but does not give to ascetics. The third adds both a wholly lawful means and generous merit-making.
